description: For decades, we’ve been told that "High Availability" means keeping a warm spare in the basement. We accepted the failover windows, the data loss during "the flip," and the wasted infrastructure as the cost of doing business. But the era of the passive node is over.

In this lightning session, we are questioning everything you were taught about databases at scale. Why pay for infrastructure that does nothing? Why settle for "eventual" availability when you can have "continuous" operations?

We’ll break down why Active-Passive is a legacy constraint we no longer have to pass down to the next generation of engineers. You’ll learn how Active-Active architectures provide true resilience, linear scalability, and—most importantly—peace of mind. It’s time to stop planning for failure and start designing for constant uptime. My children will never deploy Active-Passive, and after these 15 minutes, you won't want to either.

sessions.title: A Practical Guide to JVM Native Memory in Kubernetes
description: Most JVM tuning stops at the heap, but in Kubernetes, that’s often why you’re overprovisioning memory and still getting OOMKilled. Native memory (metaspace, threads, direct buffers, and more) quietly consumes a significant portion of your container limits, leading teams to oversize requests “just to be safe” and pay for it.

In this lightning talk, we’ll break down where JVM memory really goes and show how to use built-in tools like Native Memory Tracking (NMT) and jcmd to get a clear picture in minutes. You’ll leave with a simple approach to right-size your JVM, avoid unexpected container kills, and reduce wasted memory spend.

sessions.title: Why Developers Should Love Testing
description: We know that test automation is often discussed as a “best practice” in modern software development, but why should we love automated testing as a developer? In this presentation, we will learn how reliance on manual testing and processes for validation lies at the heart of some of the most challenging problems in software development. We will then cover practices and principles for developing reliable, portable, and maintainable automated tests. This will help developers not view automated testing as a chore but as a central aspect of our work that helps us deliver better customer service!

sessions.title: It is STILL About the Data
description: AI has emphasized the critical role of a solid data strategy and effective data management. Although the requirements and technology surrounding data are constantly changing, the fundamental principles remain consistent. This presentation reviews these principles and explores the best approaches to provide dependable and efficient data solutions in the age of AI.

sessions.title: Can We Make $1 Million in the Next Hour? (Live-Coding a Full-Stack App)
description: Can we make a $1 million? Probably not, but we can deploy a whole app! In this live-coding session, we will attempt the "impossible": going from a blank editor to a deployed, database-backed application with a functional UI before the session timer runs out.

This isn't a get-rich-quick scheme; This is a crash course on how to vibe code your way to success: we will use Claude and Gemini, NotebookLM to generate ideas, OpenArt for assets, and our favorite agents to generate our documentation on the fly.
While all can benefit from this session, it's designed for those who are skeptical or intimidated by agentic workflows, this session will cover:
The Product Manager Mindset: How to prompt for architecture, not just syntax. We will discuss the "Accept All" trap and how to spot hallucinations before they break production.
The Live Stack: A look at the specific toolchain for 2026 rapid deployment that makes this speed possible.
The Reality Check: We won't just show the happy path. We will do live debugging and discuss the security implications of shipping AI-generated code.

We'll crowdsource the app idea from a curated list at the start of the hour. Will we walk away millionaires? We can hope. Will you walk away knowing exactly how to build your next big idea? Definitely.

sessions.title: A Data-Driven Approach to Mental Health
description: I suffer from bipolar disorder. I have struggled with depression, anxiety, and mania. My mania has affected my relationship with my wife, while the other two has caused me trouble at work including getting fired. But through it all I am happy with my life, because I know what to expect during depression and mania and I have a plan.

During my presentation that I have given to 5 meetups, I explore a little bit of my history, some definitions, some symptoms I feel, some tools I use, the plan I have, some videos, my thoughts on AI therapy, and then the meaning of life.

sessions.title: The Real Race Begins After Go-Live: Mastering Long-Term Operations for Max Value
description: The launch of a new system isn’t the finish line, it’s the green flag waving to signal the start of a new race to prove value and return on investment. The business won’t wait for platform stabilization. Transformations missing the nuance of post-launch operations start on the wrong foot - quickly spinning into negative opinions and dwindling organizational confidence regarding the initiative’s efforts and purpose. Attendees will leave with a readiness checklist to launch with maximum velocity.

sessions.title: Build for Every Screen with Flutter
description: Building for mobile and web used to mean managing fragmented codebases, writing boilerplate, and wrestling with UI frameworks disconnected from your backend. In this demo-heavy session, we’ll dive into how Flutter and Dart fundamentally change that workflow. We won't just look at how to build beautiful, natively compiled apps from a single codebase—we’ll explore how using Dart on both the server and client allows you to completely eliminate duplicate code by sharing data models, validation logic, and business rules across your entire stack.

Watch live as we leverage Flutter's Hot Reload to build an interactive application from a blank canvas. You'll see exactly how easy it is to wire up shared backend data models, handle complex state management on the fly, and polish it off with buttery-smooth animations.

sessions.title: The Data Product Revolution
description: Most organizations don’t have a data problem. They have a trust problem.
​We’ve built faster pipelines, cheaper storage, and prettier dashboards. And yet teams still argue over numbers, rebuild the same datasets, and don’t trust what’s already there.
​We be walking through what “Data as a Product” actually means in practice:
- ​Why ownership is the missing ingredient
- ​Why governance keeps failing when it’s bolted on
- ​How trust, reuse, and speed are designed, not hoped for
- ​How to start without a massive transformation program
​This isn’t theory or vendor hype. It’s a practical operating model for teams that want data people actually trust and reuse.

sessions.title: Happy Hour
Building an Agent Harness for Production in Production: The story of AURA
description: In this talk we'll walk through the story of AURA, an apache 2 licensed agent harness for running production operations. Agent harnesses provide an opinionated way to enforce guardrails, memory, and tool calling without needing to define logic or have a full SDLC for your agents. As the number of agents running in production increase the value of a reliable harness increases as well which is why we released AURA to push AI-SRE into the open in a way that didn't require the normal amount of boilerplate code to make them production-ready in the end. We'll also cover challenges involved with complex multi-agent workflows and tool calls, and how we solved this inside of AURA.

sessions.title: GPU Acceleration in Data Analytics
description: High-performance analytics is increasingly critical for enterprise AI and agentic workloads ingesting massive quantities of structured data. GPU acceleration with cuDF offers a practical path to faster analytics through familiar dataframe and SQL interfaces. With open-source integrations for pandas, Polars, DuckDB, Spark, and Presto, cuDF makes it easier to adopt GPU-powered analytics within existing workflows. This talk gives attendees a concrete roadmap to understand the ecosystem, identify high-impact use cases, and start accelerating analytics without a ground-up rewrite.

sessions.title: Building Innovation-Ready Teams: The DNA of High-Performing Groups
description: Innovation isn’t just about hiring smart people—it’s about creating the right conditions for them to thrive. The most successful teams don’t just generate ideas; they experiment, iterate, and execute with speed and confidence. But what makes some teams highly innovative while others struggle with bureaucracy, misalignment, or stagnation?

This session will break down the DNA of high-performing, innovation-ready teams. You’ll learn the key elements of team design, leadership, and culture that enable teams to take risks, collaborate effectively, and consistently deliver breakthrough results.

Whether you’re a leader looking to level up your team’s innovation capabilities or a team member seeking to improve collaboration, this session will give you a practical framework to build teams that move fast, think boldly, and innovate with purpose.
Key Topics:
🔹 The Science of High-Performing Teams – What research reveals about the best innovation teams
🔹 Psychological Safety & Trust – The foundation of creative problem-solving and risk-taking
🔹 Balancing Autonomy & Alignment – How to give teams freedom while keeping them focused on shared goals
🔹 The Role of Leadership in Innovation – How great leaders set the stage for bold thinking and execution
🔹 Collaboration & Cross-Functionality – Breaking down silos to drive faster decision-making and execution
🔹 Agile & Lean Thinking in Teams – How iterative approaches fuel speed and adaptability
🔹 Sustaining an Innovation Culture – Turning one-time successes into long-term team capabilities
Key Takeaways:
✅ A Blueprint for Innovation-Ready Teams – Learn the core principles of team design that enable innovation to thrive
✅ Practical Strategies for Leaders & Teams – Gain actionable tools to improve collaboration, creativity, and execution
✅ Techniques for Building Psychological Safety – Create an environment where people feel safe to share ideas and take risks
✅ Stronger, More Aligned Teams – Understand how to structure teams for maximum impact and innovation success

sessions.title: From Java to AI: Modernizing Enterprise Systems with Machine Learning
description: Java has been the backbone of enterprise software for decades — but in today's world, AI and Machine Learning are redefining what enterprise systems can do. The question is: how do you bridge the two?

In this session, Surya Rao Rayarao — Lead Software Engineer at SS&C Technologies, IEEE Senior Member, and MS Data Science graduate (UT Austin) — draws on 20+ years of Java and enterprise engineering experience to show you exactly how to evolve modern Java applications with AI/ML capabilities, without a full rewrite.
Key takeaways:
• The evolution of Java enterprise systems: from J2EE to AI-ready architectures
• Practical patterns for embedding ML pipelines into Spring Boot and Java microservices
• Real-world FinTech examples: using AI to solve complex financial data challenges in Java-based systems
• How to expose ML models as REST APIs and integrate them with existing Java backends
• Career insights for Java engineers looking to evolve into AI/ML-integrated roles

Whether you're a Java developer curious about AI, a tech lead navigating modernization, or an architect designing next-gen systems, this talk delivers actionable strategies grounded in 20+ years of real production Java experience.

sessions.title: Living in a Stream
description: Master the Gemini Live API. Build "full-duplex" agents that can see gestures and hear commands with zero-latency, allowing for true real-time, interruptible interaction.

sessions.title: Blazor Fundamentals: Getting Started with Modern .NET Web Development
description: Blazor lets .NET developers build interactive, full-featured web applications using C#, bringing modern web development into your existing .NET ecosystem. This session is designed for developers new to Blazor who want a practical, hands-on introduction to the framework.

We’ll walk through setting up your development environment, exploring project structure, and creating your first Blazor app. You’ll learn about render modes, from static server-side rendering to the latest Interactive Auto mode. You’ll also see how to work with forms and manage data effectively. You’ll learn how to leverage the NavigationManager to make routing simple and pass data between pages. Finally, you’ll learn to design reusable components that provide the backbone for robust, maintainable applications.
Along the way, we’ll explore the Blazor component lifecycle, event handling, and performance best practices to help you create responsive and dynamic web applications.

By the end of this session, you’ll be ready to confidently build interactive Blazor applications, understand the key concepts and patterns behind components, and apply practical techniques that set you up for success in modern .NET web development.

sessions.title: Testing Infrastructure as Code - Ensuring Reliability in Terraform and CloudFormation
description: Many teams leverage infrastructure as code but don't test it. Learn how to test your infrastructure before you break production. I'll cover Terraform and CloudFormation testing tools—from linting to integration tests—with live demos including Test-Driven Infrastructure (TDI).

sessions.title: RAG Has a Relationship Problem
description: You've built a RAG pipeline. It retrieves relevant chunks, stuffs them into a prompt, and most of the time it works. Until it doesn't. The answer is somewhere in your documents, but your system keeps missing it, or worse, it confidently stitches together pieces that don't belong together. The problem often isn't your embeddings or your model. It's that vector search is great at finding similar content, but terrible at following relationships: that these two chunks are about the same person, that this policy supersedes that one, that steps A, B, and C have to happen in order.

Graphs fix the relationship problem. Not by replacing your existing stack, but by giving it the connective tissue it's been missing. We'll start from zero on graph concepts, so no prior experience required, then get practical: how do you add a knowledge graph to a retrieval pipeline without rebuilding everything from scratch, and what kinds of questions suddenly become answerable that weren't before?
You'll leave with a clear mental model of what graphs bring to retrieval, a realistic picture of the implementation complexity, and a decision framework for whether your use case is a good fit.

sessions.title: When Logging Becomes The Outage: Escaping the ECS Logging Trap
description: Logging systems are designed to help us understand failures, but what happens when the Logging itself becomes the cause of an outage?

In this session, I will walk through a real-world incident involving Amazon ECS where the default logging configuration used blocking mode with CloudWatch as the log destination. When CloudWatch experienced an outage, application containers continued attempting to push logs while buffering them locally. As the logging buffer reached its limit, containers became blocked waiting for the logging driver, ultimately impacting application availability.

This talk explores how a seemingly harmless default configuration can create an unexpected reliability risk in distributed systems. We will look at how ECS logging works under the hood, why blocking mode can create cascading failures during downstream outages, and how switching to non-blocking mode can isolate application workloads from logging system failures.

I will share the investigation process, architectural decisions, and practical lessons learned from redesigning the logging strategy to prevent observability dependencies from affecting production workloads.

Attendees will leave with actionable guidance on designing resilient logging pipelines and avoiding a class of failures where logging infrastructure unintentionally becomes the single point of failure.

sessions.title: From Claims to Copilots: Architecting AI-Ready Operational Systems
description: Many organizations are eager to adopt AI, but few have the operational data architecture required to support it in production systems.

In real environments, critical workflow data is scattered across transactional systems, operational tools, and analytics platforms that rarely share a common model. Without a coherent operational architecture, AI tools struggle to reason about workflow state or produce meaningful insights.
This session explores how operational lifecycle modeling can create the foundation for AI-enabled systems.

Using a healthcare revenue cycle environment as a case study, we’ll examine how operational events can be captured in Microsoft Dataverse and unified with analytics in Microsoft Fabric to create a canonical operational model. This architecture allows AI copilots and automation tools to reason about the state of real-world workflows rather than disconnected data points.
Attendees will learn:
Why many AI initiatives fail when they start with models instead of architecture
How lifecycle-based data modeling improves observability of operational systems
How platforms like Dataverse and Microsoft Fabric can support AI-ready architectures
Rather than focusing on AI theory or tools alone, this session focuses on the operational systems design required to make AI useful in complex real-world environments.

sessions.title: Always Let Your Context Be Your Guide
description: In our quest for "best practices", we often forget that what works brilliantly in a large software company might fail spectacularly in a small to medium size business or startup. Practices that literally save lives and improve quality for one team can be a waste of time for another. This talk shares at least twenty-five contextual elements (references to them online will be shared, we will only cover a few during the presentation) that can impact everything from your choice of software methodology to the amount of time a developer should spend trying to make a function run faster. Functional requirements, business regulations, security demands, deployment frequency, and architecture, are just a few of the elements that should inform our technical decisions. Should you use TDD? Should you provide estimates? Should you automate deployments? Should you hold retrospectives? All these questions and more can be answered once you identify your context. Through examples based on real-world experiences, research, and learning from others, you'll gain new perspectives for evaluating your unique development context and making decisions that work for you, rather than blindly following what worked for someone else.

sessions.title: CPU & GPU: Analytics Benchmarks with DuckDB & SiriusDB
description: GPU acceleration is rapidly becoming a focal point for analytical workloads—but how much does it actually help in real-world scenarios?

In this talk, we present a hands-on evaluation of GPU-accelerated analytics using industry benchmarks across multiple execution engines, including DuckDB and emerging GPU-native systems like SiriusDB. We focus on reproducible experiments and practical deployment constraints.

We explore how performance varies across query types, data layouts, and storage formats, highlighting where GPUs deliver significant gains—and where they fall short. Along the way, we examine key factors such as memory pressure, data transfer overhead, and the interaction between indexing strategies and execution engines.

Attendees will leave with a clear understanding of when GPU acceleration is worth the investment, how to design meaningful benchmarks, and what to watch out for when bringing GPUs into lakehouse analytics environments.

sessions.title: Coding Paradise: The Future of App Creation with .NET MAUI
description: Dive into cross-platform app development with .NET MAUI, Microsoft's Multi-platform App UI framework. Learn how MAUI allows you to craft native mobile and desktop applications using C# and XAML. You'll be able to unify your development efforts for Android, iOS, macOS, and Windows under a single shared codebase while still enabling access to every aspect of each native platform. Unlock the potential of .NET MAUI, where the creation of cross-platform applications becomes an accessible reality.

sessions.title: Cloud Cost Efficiency as an Operating Principle
description: Many organizations are able to deliver reliable, secure infrastructure for developers to consume. Cloud costs often come in as an after thought, however. This leads to a feast or famine pattern of not thinking about cloud costs until they spiral out of control. By failing to prioritize cost efficiency as an operating principle, platform teams distract themselves when bill blow-outs do occur, while wasting profit dollars along the way.
In this talk we will discuss:
- The cultural foundations needed for a cost efficient cloud footprint
- The foundational processes that enable cost optimization initiatives
- How to prioritize different cost optimization initiatives
- Tactical ways, from experience, to save in the cloud across compute, storage, and networking

sessions.title: Data Without Borders: The Era of the Open Lakehouse
description: We just entered a new era of the deconstructed database, the walls are coming down and data storage is no longer connected to a query engine or proprietary data format. The future of data isn't just about open storage or open source software - it’s about interoperability.

In this talk, we explore how Apache Iceberg has evolved from a table format into the “universal mesh” that connects the modern data stack. We will dive into the architectural shift from fragile ETL pipelines to seamless, multi-engine access. Discover how data powerhouses like AWS S3, Databricks, Postgres, Snowflake, DuckDB, Clickhouse, and so many others are being reimagined as "Iceberg-native" through logical replication and REST catalogs.
Join us to map out a future where data is no longer a prisoner of its platform - but a liquid asset accessible to any engine, at any time.

sessions.title: What You Need to Know (And Why You Should Care) About AI Governance
description: AI governance is no longer just for your legal team, but is becoming a daily reality for developers and platform engineers. The rapid adoption of AI agents taking real-world actions introduces an entirely new risk profile for everyone on the product team.
But what does "governance" actually look like when you’re debugging an agent's reasoning loop or trying to hit a sprint deadline without getting blocked?

This session skips legal theory to focus on what product teams actually need to know. We’ll look at how to translate high-level guidelines like NIST’s AI Risk Management Framework and the EU AI Act into practical engineering decisions. We will use a beginner friendly governance framework as a lens on how to balance innovation with accountability, helping your team navigate: what we need to do for the product, what we should do ethically, what we must do legally, and what we can do technically.
Whether you’re writing code or managing the roadmap, you’ll leave with practical strategies to build systems that are resilient, compliant, and ready for global deployment.

sessions.title: Right-Sizing Your Analytics Architecture: From Laptop to Lakehouse
description: In the analytics world, we often face a challenging dilemma: build too small and you'll hit scaling walls; build too big and you'll waste resources on unnecessary complexity. This talk presents a pragmatic approach to building analytics systems that can start small but grow seamlessly to enterprise scale. We'll demonstrate how modern open-source tools like Polars, Postgres and DuckDB paired with cloud-native storage formats create a pathway to scale without overengineering your initial implementation.

Many data teams struggle with the tension between immediate needs and future scalability. Traditional approaches often force an either/or decision: either build for today (and rewrite later) or build for tomorrow (and delay value delivery). This talk challenges that false dichotomy by showcasing a flexible architecture that evolves naturally from single-node to distributed processing with minimal friction.

We'll walk through a real-world analytics pipeline that begins on a single machine using lightweight, high-performance tools and then seamlessly transitions to distributed computing as data volumes grow. The key insight is that by making smart choices about data formats and storage from the beginning, you can postpone many scaling decisions without creating technical debt.
Key Topics
* The Scalability Spectrum: Understanding when single-node processing is sufficient and when distributed systems become necessary
* Starting Small: Leveraging Polars, Postgres and DuckDB for lightning-fast analytics on a single node
* Open Table Formats: How Apache Iceberg over S3 provides a foundation for future scale
* The Bridge to Big: Using GPU acceleration to extend single-node capabilities
* Going Distributed: Transitioning to Databricks, Snowflake, or other distributed systems with the same data
* Decision Framework: How to make architectural choices that don't paint you into a corner
Attendees will learn:
1. How to build analytics systems that start small but can grow to petabyte scale
2. Practical techniques for avoiding premature optimization while ensuring future scalability
3. When to use single-node vs. distributed processing tools
4. How modern open table formats enable seamless transitions between processing engines
5. A decision framework for making pragmatic architecture choices

This talk is designed for data engineers, analytics engineers, and architects who want to build systems that deliver immediate value while supporting future growth. It's ideal for teams that are starting new analytics initiatives or looking to modernize existing pipelines.

sessions.title: Look Ma, No Backend! Building Secure, Dynamic, and Hybrid Apps with Google's Firebase AI Logic
description: The modern app developer's dream is simple: build intelligent, multimodal features without the burden of spinning up, scaling, and maintaining a dedicated backend server. Firebase AI Logic makes this a reality by giving client SDKs direct, secure access to Google's latest Gemini 3 models. But moving generative AI entirely to the client-side introduces a scary new Wild West: how do you secure your API quota from malicious users? How do you update prompt templates or swap models without waiting days for an app store review? And what happens when your user steps into a cellular dead zone?

In this code-forward session, we’ll build and stress-test a live, client-side AI application right from the podium. We’ll explore the crucial architectural guardrails required to run client-side AI safely in production, and what Google's Firebase brings to the table to help solve these problems.

sessions.title: No More Opt-Outs: Mastering Resizability and Orientation in Android 17
description: With the release of Android 17 (API 37), the era of "locking" your UI is coming to an end. The platform is removing the developer opt-out for orientation and resizability restrictions on large screens, making adaptive layouts a requirement rather than a choice.

How do you transition a legacy codebase to a world of fluid windowing? In this session, we will dive into the technical solutions for supporting landscape, portrait, and multi-window environments. We’ll cover how to handle configuration changes gracefully, leverage WindowSizeClasses, and ensure your app remains functional and beautiful across the entire Android ecosystem.

sessions.title: AI: The Agile Manifesto's Final Form
description: Twenty-five years ago, seventeen developers declared that working software matters more than process. Then we spent a quarter century turning Agile into the very bureaucracy it was designed to replace.
Then AI-enabled engineering changed everything, including Agile, because AI is the fulfilment of Agile's promise.
"Working software over documentation" becomes real when AI collapses the distance between intent and running code to minutes.
"Responding to change" stops being expensive advice when regenerating a component costs minutes instead of days.
"Customer collaboration" transforms when you can prototype in real time instead of promising a demo next sprint.
"Individuals over process" finally lands when AI amplifies engineering judgment instead of burying it in ceremony.

But there's a catch. Agile without discipline gave us chaos wearing a manifesto as a hall pass. AI without discipline gives us vibe coding dressed as innovation. It's the same failure in a shinier package.
Attendees will learn how AI embraces all the ideals of Agile and how to implement AI with the right amount of discipline to deliver on time and with quality.

sessions.title: The Most Secure Platform is the one People Use
description: The world is full of examples where people bypass elaborate edifices designed by smart, well-meaning experts. Security teams love technically perfect solutions, but often spend too little time on how people will actually experience them. We discuss the basics of UI/UX design and how to select security features that enhance the value of a product instead of reducing it.

sessions.title: Ignite Intro / Overview
What HTTP Can Teach Us About Better Human Communication
description: In DevOps, our systems rely on clear contracts, acknowledgements, and predictable responses - but our communication often doesn’t. The result is endless “just checking in” pings, unnecessary meetings, and avoidable interruptions.

This lightning talk applies HTTP concepts like request types, status codes, and response timing to everyday interactions. By treating communication like an API, teams can reduce ambiguity, eliminate redundant follow-ups, and create more reliable, low-noise collaboration patterns.
Walk away with a simple “human API contract” you can start using immediately.

sessions.title: Stop. Using. YAML. Anchors.
description: YAML anchors feel like a clever way to keep configuration DRY. A little &base, a quick <<: *base, and suddenly your CI config is reusable and elegant.
Until someone has to read it.
Six months later your pipeline is powered by invisible inheritance, confusing merges, and configuration indirection that makes debugging feel like archaeology.
In this lightning talk, we’ll explore why YAML anchors often make configs harder to reason about, harder to maintain, and harder to onboard engineers into—and what to do instead.
Because clever YAML is usually a mistake.

sessions.title: Show your work: AI fact-checking with versioned documentation
description: Use AI to fact-check your work code, tutorial, and documentation using versioned docs index on your machine.

sessions.title: Best Practices for Oncall Teams
description: Bad practices can sink on-call teams. On-call is hard enough without adding on drama and frustration! Help your responders have a better on-call experience by reassessing some key requirements and employing a few alternatives.

sessions.title: Lunch
Open Spaces
Closing
